key_insight: No single 3D multimodal registration method was robust across all anatomies and modalities; better overlap scores did not always mean better global image correspondence.
clinical_relevance: For clinical imaging workflows, registration quality should be judged with multiple metrics, because label overlap alone may hide misalignment in unlabeled regions.
method: Benchmarked classical optimization-based and modern learning-based deformable registration methods
Tested three datasets spanning synthetic deformation recovery and real intra-patient clinical scenarios
Compared Dice, HD95, and MIND-SSC to capture both geometric and image-based alignment
evidence_signal: Across three datasets, learning-based methods performed best on large synthetic benchmarks, while gains were limited in real pelvic cases and geometric metrics often disagreed with MIND-SSC.
watch_item: Anatomy-guided methods can boost overlap in segmented areas but may worsen global coherence outside those regions, so deployment needs careful multi-criteria validation.
paper_title: Benchmarking Intra-Patient 3D Deformable Multimodal Image Registration
